samples.summary: No test covers Parquet-native value types (INT64 BigInt, timestamps/Date, byte arrays, nested lists/structs)
samples.evidence: The unit test feeds `parquetReadObjects` a mock resolving to plain JSON-ish records (`{name:'Alice', score:95, active:true}`, parquet-importer.test.ts:24-27), so every value passed to `toCell` is a string/number/boolean — exactly the shapes already exercised by json-importer.test.ts. The only real-decode test (parquet-importer.integration.test.ts:11-28) uses a 2-row fixture whose asserted cells are 'id'→'1', 'Alice', 'FALSE'. hyparquet decodes INT64 columns as BigInt, TIMESTAMP as Date/BigInt, and LIST/STRUCT as arrays/objects; `toCell` (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:33-37) routes objects through `JSON.stringify`, which throws "Do not know how to serialize a BigInt" for a nested int64 list and yields `{"0":..}` for a Uint8Array. Nothing in the diff's tests would fail if those very common Parquet columns import as garbage or throw during import, i.e. the data-fidelity core of the new feature is untested.

samples.summary: 'Imported Parquet' fallback sheet name is never exercised by any test
samples.evidence: `importParquet` passes fallback "Imported Parquet" to `sheetImportBaseName` (sheet-import-actions.ts:119) and `importRecordsAsSheet` uses `fallbackName: 'Imported Parquet'` (packages/sheets/src/import/parquet-importer.ts:24). The frontend parquet test only uses "metrics.PARQUET" (importers.test.ts:135-146) and the sheets tests always pass a non-blank sheetName ('People'/'Empty'). The equivalent JSON fallback IS tested (json-importer.test.ts:60-63), so this path is a knowingly narrower gap: a wrong/blank tab name would ship undetected.

samples.summary: No test covers the unbounded/failure behavior of the Parquet upload path (no truncation budget, error surfacing in the upload queue)
samples.evidence: `importParquet` returns no `truncated`/`rowCount` and applies no cell budget, unlike `importCsv` whose budget passthrough is explicitly asserted (importers.test.ts:116-133). upload-queue-worker.test.ts covers a failing `.ndjson` import (line 103) but no `.parquet` case, so nothing tests what a user sees when a large or corrupt Parquet is dropped in. The new parquet test only asserts the happy-path mock call.

samples.summary: manualChunks routing of hyparquet/fzstd/hysnappy into 'sheet-core' has no unit test
samples.evidence: vite.config.ts:180-189 adds new chunk routing; grep for 'manualChunks'/'sheet-core' finds no test importing or asserting the function's output (only the config itself and docs). The chunk-count/size lane will catch gross regressions, so the impact is contained, but the mapping predicate itself (e.g. a path-substring typo) is unverified by any assertion.

samples.summary: Unit test mocks away the whole Parquet reader, so it verifies only wiring; real decode coverage rests on a single small fixture
samples.evidence: `vi.mock('hyparquet')` and `vi.mock('hyparquet-compressors')` (lines 7-13) replace the code that actually parses Parquet, leaving the test asserting the reader was called with `{file, compressors}` plus record→cell mapping already covered by json-importer tests. This is acceptable given parquet-importer.integration.test.ts decodes a real GZIP fixture, but that single fixture (3 columns, 2 rows) is the sole real-decode signal for the feature.

verdict.reason: I could not find a counterexample, but I also could not fully settle the finding. Verified facts: the parquet importer (packages/sheets/src/import/parquet-importer.ts:17-26) delegates to importRecordsAsSheet (record-importer.ts:59-71), which converts every value with toCell (store/readonly.ts:33-37) — Date→ISO, object→JSON.stringify, else String(). The unit test mocks parquetReadObjects with plain scalars only (parquet-importer.test.ts:24-27, assertions 39-53), and the only real-decode test asserts 'id'/'1'/'Alice'/'FALSE' on a 3-column DuckDB fixture (parquet-importer.integration.test.ts:9-29). Searching wider than the reviewer did, I found no test anywhere feeding BigInt, Uint8Array, or a Date through toCell/record-importer: there is no record-importer test, no toCell test, the only ReadOnlyStore test (test/store/store.test.ts:65-71) covers data-validation no-ops, and the frontend importer test mocks importParquetFile entirely (frontend/src/app/documents/__tests__/importers.test.ts:34-49,135-146). The Date coverage in csv-importer.test.ts:88-94 goes through the CSV path's own converter, not toCell; json-importer.test.ts:39-42 does cover nested object/array stringification through the same record-importer path, but JSON text cannot express BigInt or byte arrays. The residual doubt, which carries most of the finding's severity: I could not determine whether the fixture's `id` column is INT64 (DuckDB frequently emits BIGINT), in which case the integration assertion at line 22 would in fact exercise the BigInt→cell path. hyparquet is not installed in node_modules and the fixture's Thrift schema is unreadable with read-only tools, so I cannot resolve it either way.
